correctness.rationale: The count-conditioned estimator follows from standard conditional Poisson locations and the memoryless property. Exact summation yields R(z)=2-exp(-z)(1+2z+zF(z)) with F(z)=Ei(z)-EulerGamma-log z; differentiating gives R'(z)=-exp(-z)g(z), g''(z)=(1+z-exp z)/z^2<0. From g(0+)=1 and g'(0+)=0, g is strictly decreasing to -infinity and crosses once. This verifies all z>0 and both boundaries, not just a numerical optimizer. A separately derived conditional-variance series and derivative identities were replayed with Python/SymPy/mpmath. The result excludes unknown rates, noisy data, bounded horizons and multiple observations.

value.rationale: One exact counter reading has an immediate measurement-scheduling consequence for reconstructing the first arrival. The nontrivial sharp and unique scale 1.78566038/lambda and exact minimum risk 0.32173880/lambda^2 are not implied by the standard conditional-uniform calculation alone: global optimization requires the special-function curvature argument. The selected full-count design beats the independently optimal one-bit presence sensor by 8.698% in squared loss and the no-reading risk by 67.826%. This is a natural finite-information numerical approximation invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no larger downstream theorem is claimed.
